treaty_name: Convention between the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for the avoidance of double taxation with respect to taxes on income (1981), applied between the UK and Bosnia and Herzegovina by succession
eif_quote: [BA MLI] United Kingdom Original 06-11-1981 16-09-1982 || Art. 27: The Convention shall enter into force on the date of the later of these notifications and shall thereupon have effect: (a) in the United Kingdom: (i) in respect of income tax and capital gains tax, for any year of assessment beginning on or after the sixth day of April in the calendar year following that in which the later notification is received; (ii) in respect of corporation tax, for any financial year beginning on or after the first day of April in the calendar year following ...; (b) in Yugoslavia: in respect of Yugoslavia tax, for any fiscal year beginning on or after the first day of January in the calendar year following that in which the later notification is received.
source_title: gov.uk: Synthesised text of the MLI and the UK–Yugoslavia Double Taxation Convention as it applies between the UK and Bosnia and Herzegovina (official, English); also UK–Yugoslavia convention in force PDF

rates.quote: (a) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner thereof is a company (excluding a partnership) which controls directly or indirectly at least 25 per cent of the voting power in the company paying the dividends;
(b) in all other cases, 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of [this Convention], a benefit under [this Convention] shall not be granted in respect of an item of income if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of [this Convention].

notes: SFRY convention applied by succession: gov.uk Bosnia-Herzegovina tax treaties page ("Convention with Yugoslavia continues to apply"; synthesised text prepared with the BiH competent authority); BiH MoF also lists it in force. Dividend 25% test is on voting power, direct or indirect. Art. 10(3)-(4): UK tax-credit regime for portfolio dividends (deduction up to 15% of dividend plus credit) - obsolete since UK abolished payable tax credits; not modelled. valid_from: Yugoslav tax from 1 Jan 1983; UK from 6 Apr 1983 (income tax) / 1 Apr 1983 (corporation tax). MLI WHT effect 1 Jan 2021 per gov.uk synthesised text ("for taxes withheld at source, from 1 January 2021"). MLI Art. 8 not applicable (BiH reserved).
